newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Unpaid Israeli undertakers bring body to city hall.
newsitem.headline: Unpaid Israeli undertakers bring body to city hall.

text.p: Unpaid undertakers laid out their wage demands -- and a body -- at a municipal council meeting in an Israeli town buried under a pile of debt.

"'Chutzpa' (nerve) and blasphemy," Deputy Religious Affairs Minister Yigal Bibi told Israel Radio on Wednesday after workers from the Jewish burial society in Rosh Ha'ayin, near Tel Aviv, brought a woman's corpse to city hall on Tuesday evening.
The religious undertakers had not received wages from the town for three months, officials said.
"As Passover approaches, they have no money to buy food...and decided to bring the body," Menashe Madmoni, a member of the town's religious authority, told the Maariv newspaper.
"The council meeting was stopped, there was a commotion and it all ended with the corpse being buried," he said.
A photo in Maariv showed grim-faced councillors standing around the body, which was placed on a stretcher and covered with a shroud bearing the Star of David.

Rosh Ha'ayin's mayor condemned the protest but Bibi accused the town, which he said was millions of dollars in debt, of not paying the Orthodox burial workers in a bid to press Israel's religious interior minister to send it more funds.
"We will try to pay (the undertakers) directly today," Bibi said.
